title: The event that turned an aerospace engineer into an AI founder
excerpt: After her aunt's cancer diagnosis upended her family, Lily Vittayarukskul built an AI startup to help others prepare for long-term care.
content_html:
I dreamt of building rockets until my aunt's illness inspired me to build an AI startup that's raised nearly $10 million

By Jessica Orwig

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

This as-told-to essay is based on a conversation with Lily Vittayarukskul, 30, cofounder and CEO of Waterlily. It has been edited for length and clarity.

When I was a kid, I was fascinated by the universe and wanted to understand how the world worked. Science taught me that even the biggest, most intimidating questions could be broken down, understood, and eventually solved.

I also grew up with limited resources, and working in my parents' factory after school taught me how hard families work to create stability, and how much discipline and resourcefulness it takes to build something from very little.

At 11, I entered a NASA competition with a homemade water rocket, won the competition, and got the chance to visit Kennedy Space Center. Later, I interned at NASA as a young teenager. For years, I thought aerospace engineering was my future.

Then my aunt was diagnosed with cancer, and the trajectory of my entire family changed almost overnight.

My aunt didn't speak much English, so my mom translated at doctor's appointments. My family quickly learned that there were expenses we hadn't expected. We also learned that caring for someone with a serious illness extended far beyond medical appointments.

I was 16 when she became sick. What I remember most wasn't a single diagnosis or conversation. It was the quiet.

Everyone in my family was exhausted, moving from work to doctor's appointments to caregiving without ever stopping to talk about what was happening. We were all operating on autopilot because there was simply too much to do.

Watching my family unravel changed my definition of impact

My mom became my aunt's primary caregiver. The rest of us worked at the family factory whenever we could. I went to my parents' factory after school, often staying until 10 p.m. or 11 p.m. before going home.

Only later did I realize the full cost.

Our family relationships had become strained. Financially, we had almost nothing left. There was blame, tension, and isolation that lingered long after my aunt died.

Growing up in a first-generation immigrant family, I'd always understood that money mattered. My parents worked incredibly hard, yet I learned early that hard work alone doesn't guarantee financial security. You have to create economic value. That lesson shaped almost every decision I've made since.

After my aunt died, I started asking a different question: Instead of wondering how I could build better rockets, I wondered why families like mine had to navigate one of life's hardest moments with so little support.

I realized no one was solving the problem I cared about most

I still loved engineering and building things, but I realized I could apply those skills somewhere that felt much more personal.

I spent nearly a decade leading product and engineering at early-stage companies while learning everything I could about healthcare, financial services, and underserved populations. I wanted to understand why planning for aging and long-term care was so fragmented.

No one seemed to be solving the problem the way I thought it needed to be solved. That's why I cofounded Waterlily.

Waterlily is an AI-powered long-term care planning platform that helps people estimate when they may need long-term care, how much it could cost, and how to pay for it based on their health, finances, and family situation. The platform provides personalized projections and funding strategies—including insurance, savings, and caregiving plans—to help families prepare for the financial and logistical challenges of aging. Since launching, the company has raised $9.2 million.

The work has been much harder than I imagined.

Healthcare doesn't exist in one industry. Neither does aging. We work across healthcare, insurance, and financial services simultaneously, each with different incentives and different ways of operating. Every week seems to introduce a new layer of complexity.

There were plenty of moments when I questioned whether we could figure it out. What kept me going, though, was the same question I asked myself after my aunt died. If we're not solving this problem, who will?

After speaking with thousands of families, one thing surprised me. I'd assumed my family's experience was unusually devastating. Instead, I found that many families who experience serious long-term care needs face financial strain and relationship breakdowns. The details vary, but the emotional toll often looks remarkably similar.

Building this company changed how I think about my own future

Starting Waterlily has changed me in ways I didn't expect.

I've become much more financially literate than I ever thought I'd need to be. Building Waterlily has required me to develop deep expertise across insurance, retirement planning, healthcare, and financial services. Understanding aging means understanding how all of those systems — and the decisions families make within them — fit together.

Understanding aging means understanding insurance, retirement accounts, savings, investing, and how all those pieces fit together.

It's also changed how I think about responsibility.

When I was younger, I thought success meant solving interesting technical problems. Now, I think success means building something that helps people regain a sense of control during moments when life feels completely uncertain.

If my aunt were alive today, I don't think she would care very much about the technical details of the platform. But I also think she'd ask me two questions:

  1. Are you helping people?
  2. Is this business sustainable?

I'd like to think she'd be proud of both answers.

Waterlily offers a free tool on its site that provides personalized insights, based on more than half a billion data points, to better understand what aging and long-term care could look like.

sentences.zh: 我花了近十年的时间在早期公司领导产品和工程，同时学习有关医疗保健、金融服务和服务不足人群的一切知识。

sentences.en: I wanted to understand why planning for aging and long-term care was so fragmented.
sentences.zh: 我想了解为什么老龄化和长期护理规划如此分散。

blocks.html_en: No one seemed to be solving the problem the way I thought it needed to be solved. That's why I cofounded Waterlily.

sentences.en: No one seemed to be solving the problem the way I thought it needed to be solved.
sentences.zh: 似乎没有人按照我认为需要解决的方式解决问题。

sentences.en: That's why I cofounded Waterlily.
sentences.zh: 这就是我共同创立 Waterlily 的原因。

blocks.html_en: Waterlily is an AI-powered long-term care planning platform that helps people estimate when they may need long-term care, how much it could cost, and how to pay for it based on their health, finances, and family situation. The platform provides personalized projections and funding strategies—including insurance, savings, and caregiving plans—to help families prepare for the financial and logistical challenges of aging. Since launching, the company has raised $9.2 million.

sentences.en: Waterlily is an AI-powered long-term care planning platform that helps people estimate when they may need long-term care, how much it could cost, and how to pay for it based on their health, finances, and family situation.
sentences.zh: Waterlily 是一个由人工智能驱动的长期护理规划平台，可以帮助人们根据自己的健康、财务和家庭状况估计何时可能需要长期护理、需要多少费用以及如何支付。

sentences.en: The platform provides personalized projections and funding strategies—including insurance, savings, and caregiving plans—to help families prepare for the financial and logistical challenges of aging.
sentences.zh: 该平台提供个性化的预测和融资策略，包括保险、储蓄和护理计划，帮助家庭应对老龄化带来的财务和后勤挑战。

sentences.en: Since launching, the company has raised $9.2 million.
sentences.zh: 自成立以来，该公司已筹集 920 万美元。

blocks.html_en: The work has been much harder than I imagined.

sentences.en: The work has been much harder than I imagined.
sentences.zh: 工作比我想象的要辛苦得多。

blocks.html_en: Healthcare doesn't exist in one industry. Neither does aging. We work across healthcare, insurance, and financial services simultaneously, each with different incentives and different ways of operating. Every week seems to introduce a new layer of complexity.

sentences.en: Healthcare doesn't exist in one industry.
sentences.zh: 医疗保健并不存在于某一行业。

sentences.en: Neither does aging.
sentences.zh: 衰老也没有。

sentences.en: We work across healthcare, insurance, and financial services simultaneously, each with different incentives and different ways of operating.
sentences.zh: 我们同时在医疗保健、保险和金融服务领域开展业务，每个领域都有不同的激励措施和不同的运营方式。

sentences.en: Every week seems to introduce a new layer of complexity.
sentences.zh: 似乎每周都会引入新的复杂性。

blocks.html_en: There were plenty of moments when I questioned whether we could figure it out. What kept me going, though, was the same question I asked myself after my aunt died. If we're not solving this problem, who will?

sentences.en: There were plenty of moments when I questioned whether we could figure it out.
sentences.zh: 很多时候我都怀疑我们是否能解决这个问题。

sentences.en: What kept me going, though, was the same question I asked myself after my aunt died.
sentences.zh: 然而，让我坚持下去的，是我姨妈去世后我问自己的同样的问题。

sentences.en: If we're not solving this problem, who will?
sentences.zh: 如果我们不解决这个问题，谁来解决？

blocks.html_en: After speaking with thousands of families, one thing surprised me. I'd assumed my family's experience was unusually devastating. Instead, I found that many families who experience serious long-term care needs face financial strain and relationship breakdowns. The details vary, but the emotional toll often looks remarkably similar.

sentences.en: After speaking with thousands of families, one thing surprised me.
sentences.zh: 在与数千个家庭交谈后，有一件事让我感到惊讶。

sentences.en: I'd assumed my family's experience was unusually devastating.
sentences.zh: 我原以为我家人的经历非同寻常地具有毁灭性。

sentences.en: Instead, I found that many families who experience serious long-term care needs face financial strain and relationship breakdowns.
sentences.zh: 相反，我发现许多经历严重长期护理需求的家庭面临着经济压力和关系破裂。

sentences.en: The details vary, but the emotional toll often looks remarkably similar.
sentences.zh: 细节各不相同，但情感损失往往看起来非常相似。

blocks.html_en: Building this company changed how I think about my own future

sentences.en: Building this company changed how I think about my own future
sentences.zh: 创办这家公司改变了我对自己未来的看法

blocks.html_en: Starting Waterlily has changed me in ways I didn't expect.

sentences.en: Starting Waterlily has changed me in ways I didn't expect.
sentences.zh: 开始睡莲以我意想不到的方式改变了我。

blocks.html_en: I've become much more financially literate than I ever thought I'd need to be. Building Waterlily has required me to develop deep expertise across insurance, retirement planning, healthcare, and financial services. Understanding aging means understanding how all of those systems — and the decisions families make within them — fit together.

sentences.en: I've become much more financially literate than I ever thought I'd need to be.
sentences.zh: 我的财务知识比我想象的要高得多。

sentences.en: Building Waterlily has required me to develop deep expertise across insurance, retirement planning, healthcare, and financial services.
sentences.zh: 打造睡莲需要我在保险、退休计划、医疗保健和金融服务方面积累深厚的专业知识。

sentences.en: Understanding aging means understanding how all of those systems — and the decisions families make within them — fit together.
sentences.zh: 了解老龄化意味着了解所有这些系统以及家庭在其中做出的决定如何结合在一起。

blocks.html_en: Understanding aging means understanding insurance, retirement accounts, savings, investing, and how all those pieces fit together.

sentences.en: Understanding aging means understanding insurance, retirement accounts, savings, investing, and how all those pieces fit together.
sentences.zh: 了解老龄化意味着了解保险、退休账户、储蓄、投资以及所有这些部分如何组合在一起。

blocks.html_en: It's also changed how I think about responsibility.

sentences.en: It's also changed how I think about responsibility.
sentences.zh: 这也改变了我对责任的看法。

blocks.html_en: When I was younger, I thought success meant solving interesting technical problems. Now, I think success means building something that helps people regain a sense of control during moments when life feels completely uncertain.

sentences.en: When I was younger, I thought success meant solving interesting technical problems.
sentences.zh: 当我年轻的时候，我认为成功意味着解决有趣的技术问题。

sentences.en: Now, I think success means building something that helps people regain a sense of control during moments when life feels completely uncertain.
sentences.zh: 现在，我认为成功意味着建立一些东西，帮助人们在生活感到完全不确定的时刻重新获得控制感。

blocks.html_en: If my aunt were alive today, I don't think she would care very much about the technical details of the platform. But I also think she'd ask me two questions:

sentences.en: If my aunt were alive today, I don't think she would care very much about the technical details of the platform.
sentences.zh: 如果我姑姑今天还活着，我想她不会太关心平台的技术细节。

sentences.en: But I also think she'd ask me two questions:
sentences.zh: 但我也认为她会问我两个问题：

blocks.html_en: • Are you helping people?

sentences.en: Are you helping people?
sentences.zh: 你在帮助别人吗？

blocks.html_en: • Is this business sustainable?

sentences.en: Is this business sustainable?
sentences.zh: 这个生意可持续吗？

blocks.html_en: I'd like to think she'd be proud of both answers.

sentences.en: I'd like to think she'd be proud of both answers.
sentences.zh: 我想她会对这两个答案感到自豪。

blocks.html_en: Waterlily offers a free tool on its site that provides personalized insights, based on more than half a billion data points, to better understand what aging and long-term care could look like.

sentences.en: Waterlily offers a free tool on its site that provides personalized insights, based on more than half a billion data points, to better understand what aging and long-term care could look like.

我梦想着建造火箭，直到我姨妈的病启发我建立了一家筹集了近 1000 万美元资金的人工智能初创公司

作者：Jessica Orwig 您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。

这篇众所周知的文章基于与 30 岁的 Waterlily 联合创始人兼首席执行官 Lily Vittayarukskul 的对话。 为了篇幅和清晰度，对其进行了编辑。

当我还是个孩子的时候，我对宇宙很着迷，想了解世界是如何运作的。 科学告诉我，即使是最大、最令人生畏的问题也可以被分解、理解并最终得到解决。

我在资源有限的情况下长大，放学后在父母的工厂工作，教会了我家庭如何努力创造稳定，以及需要多少纪律和足智多谋才能从小事做起。

11岁时，我用自制的水火箭参加了NASA的比赛，赢得了比赛，并有机会参观肯尼迪航天中心。 后来，我十几岁时在美国宇航局实习。 多年来，我一直认为航空航天工程是我的未来。

然后我的姨妈被诊断出患有癌症，我整个家庭的轨迹几乎在一夜之间发生了变化。

我阿姨不太会说英语，所以我妈妈在看医生时做翻译。 我的家人很快了解到有一些我们没有预料到的费用。 我们还了解到，照顾患有严重疾病的人远远超出了医疗预约的范围。

她生病时我16岁。 我最记得的不是一次诊断或谈话。 这是安静。

我家里的每个人都精疲力竭，从工作到预约医生再到护理，却从未停下来谈论发生的事情。 我们都处于自动驾驶状态，因为要做的事情太多了。

看着我的家庭崩溃改变了我对影响的定义

我妈妈成了我姨妈的主要照顾者。 我们其他人只要有时间就在家庭工厂工作。 放学后我就去父母的工厂，经常待到晚上10点。 或晚上 11 点 回家之前。

直到后来我才意识到全部成本。

我们的家庭关系变得紧张。 在经济上，我们几乎一无所有。 在我姨妈去世后很长一段时间里，责备、紧张和孤立一直挥之不去。

我在第一代移民家庭长大，一直都明白金钱的重要性。 我的父母工作非常努力，但我很早就知道，单靠努力工作并不能保证经济安全。 你必须创造经济价值。 那次教训几乎影响了我此后所做的每一个决定。

我姨妈去世后，我开始问一个不同的问题：我不知道如何建造更好的火箭，而是想知道为什么像我这样的家庭必须在如此少的支持下度过生命中最艰难的时刻之一。

我意识到没有人能解决我最关心的问题

我仍然喜欢工程和建筑，但我意识到我可以将这些技能应用到更个人化的地方。

我花了近十年的时间在早期公司领导产品和工程，同时学习有关医疗保健、金融服务和服务不足人群的一切知识。 我想了解为什么老龄化和长期护理规划如此分散。

似乎没有人按照我认为需要解决的方式解决问题。 这就是我共同创立 Waterlily 的原因。

Waterlily 是一个由人工智能驱动的长期护理规划平台，可以帮助人们根据自己的健康、财务和家庭状况估计何时可能需要长期护理、需要多少费用以及如何支付。 该平台提供个性化的预测和融资策略，包括保险、储蓄和护理计划，帮助家庭应对老龄化带来的财务和后勤挑战。 自成立以来，该公司已筹集 920 万美元。

工作比我想象的要辛苦得多。

医疗保健并不存在于某一行业。 衰老也没有。 我们同时在医疗保健、保险和金融服务领域开展业务，每个领域都有不同的激励措施和不同的运营方式。 似乎每周都会引入新的复杂性。

很多时候我都怀疑我们是否能解决这个问题。 然而，让我坚持下去的，是我姨妈去世后我问自己的同样的问题。 如果我们不解决这个问题，谁来解决？

在与数千个家庭交谈后，有一件事让我感到惊讶。 我原以为我家人的经历非同寻常地具有毁灭性。 相反，我发现许多经历严重长期护理需求的家庭面临着经济压力和关系破裂。 细节各不相同，但情感损失往往看起来非常相似。

创办这家公司改变了我对自己未来的看法

开始睡莲以我意想不到的方式改变了我。

我的财务知识比我想象的要高得多。 打造睡莲需要我在保险、退休计划、医疗保健和金融服务方面积累深厚的专业知识。 了解老龄化意味着了解所有这些系统以及家庭在其中做出的决定如何结合在一起。

了解老龄化意味着了解保险、退休账户、储蓄、投资以及所有这些部分如何组合在一起。

这也改变了我对责任的看法。

当我年轻的时候，我认为成功意味着解决有趣的技术问题。 现在，我认为成功意味着建立一些东西，帮助人们在生活感到完全不确定的时刻重新获得控制感。

如果我姑姑今天还活着，我想她不会太关心平台的技术细节。 但我也认为她会问我两个问题：

  1. 你在帮助别人吗？
  2. 这个生意可持续吗？

我想她会对这两个答案感到自豪。

Waterlily 在其网站上提供了一款免费工具，可根据超过 5 亿个数据点提供个性化见解，以更好地了解老龄化和长期护理的情况。
